summary: Polyphony Digital's PlayStation racing-simulation series; archive choices favor the original platform for each entry, using emulator/upscale routes for legacy hardware and PS5 for cross-generation releases.

entries.title: Gran Turismo

emulation.notes: Use internal-resolution upscaling and PGXP-style geometry correction if desired.

primary.why: The first Gran Turismo shipped only on PlayStation, so the best archive route is the original version through a high-quality PS1 setup or emulator.
primary.how_to_play: Play the original PlayStation disc/image on DuckStation or original hardware; use internal-resolution scaling and a wheel/controller profile if emulating.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official remaster is sourced; preserve the original release.

entries.title: Gran Turismo 2

emulation.notes: Use internal-resolution upscaling; keep both discs configured.

primary.why: Gran Turismo 2 shipped on PlayStation only; the original two-disc package is the complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the original PlayStation release in DuckStation or on original hardware; keep both Arcade and Simulation discs available.

entries.remaster_caveats: Use the full two-disc release; no official remaster is sourced.

emulation.notes: Use a stable renderer and high internal resolution.

primary.why: Gran Turismo 3: A-Spec shipped on PlayStation 2 only; PCSX2 provides the highest-fidelity archive route for that release.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 release with PCSX2 at high internal resolution, or on original PS2 hardware with component output.

entries.title: Gran Turismo Concept

emulation.notes: Use PAL-compatible settings for the Tokyo-Geneva release.

primary.why: The Tokyo-Geneva edition is a PS2 concept-car-focused release; it is the latest broad public Concept variant covered here.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 Tokyo-Geneva release with PCSX2, ideally using a PAL-compatible setup and high internal resolution.

entries.remaster_caveats: Regional content variants exist; no official remaster is sourced.

entries.title: Gran Turismo 4 Prologue

primary.why: Gran Turismo 4 Prologue is a shorter PS2 preview release; PCSX2 is the highest-fidelity route for preserving it as its own entry.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 Prologue release in PCSX2 at high internal resolution.

entries.remaster_caveats: Play Gran Turismo 4 separately for the full game; preserve Prologue as a distinct historical release.

entries.title: Gran Turismo 4

emulation.notes: Use high internal resolution and stable renderer settings.

primary.why: Gran Turismo 4 shipped on PlayStation 2 only and is the complete follow-up to Prologue; PCSX2 gives the highest output fidelity.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS2 release in PCSX2 at high internal resolution, or on original hardware with component output.

entries.remaster_caveats: The standard release removed the planned online mode; the separate Online Test Version is cataloged separately.

entries.title: Gran Turismo 4 Online Test Version

emulation.notes: Use only for offline preservation of the test client.

primary.why: This limited PS2 test version preserves the online-mode experiment that did not ship in standard Gran Turismo 4, although public online services ended in 2006.
primary.how_to_play: Preserve only from an original test disc/image; online functions are historical and cannot be treated as currently playable.

entries.remaster_caveats: Not a replacement for the full Gran Turismo 4 release; online functionality is defunct.

entries.title: Gran Turismo HD Concept

emulation.notes: If legally preserved, PS3 emulation may be used; original PS3 install is the cleanest preservation route.

primary.why: Gran Turismo HD Concept was a free PS3 download and the first Gran Turismo release on PS3; preserve it as a historical demo rather than a full game replacement.
primary.how_to_play: Use an original PS3 install if already preserved; PlayStation Store availability is historical.

entries.remaster_caveats: Catalog as a historical demo; do not substitute it for Gran Turismo 5.

entries.title: Gran Turismo 5 Prologue

emulation.notes: Original PS3 hardware remains a straightforward route.

primary.why: Gran Turismo 5 Prologue shipped for PS3 only and is a distinct precursor to Gran Turismo 5.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS3 release on original hardware or RPCS3 if compatibility is acceptable for the target build.

entries.remaster_caveats: Preserve separately as a prologue, not as the definitive GT5 route.

primary.why: The 2009 handheld Gran Turismo shipped for PSP; PPSSPP provides the highest-fidelity archive route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PSP release with PPSSPP at high internal resolution, or on original PSP hardware.

entries.title: Gran Turismo 5

emulation.notes: Original PS3 with patches is the safest completeness route; RPCS3 may be used only if compatibility is verified.

primary.why: Gran Turismo 5 shipped for PS3 only; a fully patched PS3 install is the most complete stable route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on a patched PS3 install, preserving update data and DLC where legally owned.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official modern remaster is sourced.

entries.title: Gran Turismo 6

emulation.notes: Original PS3 with patches is the safest completeness route; RPCS3 may be used only if compatibility is verified.

primary.why: Gran Turismo 6 shipped for PS3 only; a fully patched PS3 install is the most complete stable route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on a patched PS3 install, preserving update data and DLC where legally owned.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official modern remaster is sourced.

entries.title: Gran Turismo Sport

emulation.notes: Use PS4 hardware or PS5 backward compatibility.

primary.why: Gran Turismo Sport shipped on PS4 only; online services ended in 2024, so the best archive route is the final patched offline-capable build.
primary.how_to_play: Play the final patched PS4 build on PS4 or PS5 backward compatibility, focusing on offline modes that remain playable.

entries.remaster_caveats: Not a full replacement for live Gran Turismo Sport because online features are gone; Gran Turismo 7 is the current live-series route.

entries.title: Gran Turismo 7

primary.why: Gran Turismo 7 shipped on PS4 and PS5; PS5 has the higher fidelity route with 4K/60, ray tracing features, DualSense features, faster loading, and optional PS VR2 support.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PS5 version with current updates installed; use PS VR2 optionally for VR-supported modes.

entries.remaster_caveats: Live-service/current-update state matters; preserve patch version when archiving.

entries.title: My First Gran Turismo

primary.why: My First Gran Turismo is available on PS4 and PS5; PS5 is the higher-fidelity route and includes optional PS VR2 support.
primary.how_to_play: Download the free PS5 version from PlayStation Store; treat it as an introductory GT7-derived release, not a replacement for Gran Turismo 7.

entries.remaster_caveats: Catalog separately because it is a free introductory version derived from Gran Turismo 7.
